beats.care: If you're a medical student, one wrong key can shift your rank and your PG seat. This case could set transparency rules for future exams.
beats.what: The Democratic Medical Association has asked the Supreme Court to quash an NBEMS notice that keeps actual questions and options hidden from NEET-PG 2026 candidates.
beats.why: Candidates see only a question ID, the correct option's number and their own response. Without the text, they can't spot a wrong answer key.

cards.body: The exam was held on 30 August and results came out on 24 September. The plea wants downloadable records for each candidate, a window to object to questions, an expert panel to decide objections, and corrected ranks where errors are found.
It's the official list of correct answers. Many exams publish a provisional key first and let students challenge mistakes before results are final.

cards.body: The plea was filed under Article 32, which lets citizens go straight to the Supreme Court when a fundamental right is at stake.

hook: NEET-PG takers can't see their *own questions*. Is that fair?

learn.t: NEET-PG candidates only see question IDs and answer numbers, so they can't check whether a question or its key was wrong.

tldr: Doctors who took NEET-PG 2026 have asked the Supreme Court to make NBEMS show candidates the actual questions and options, not just ID numbers.
watch: Watch for when the Supreme Court takes up the plea, and whether it says anything about counselling going ahead.
